subject: Deckhand dedicated pool: follow-up on GPU mix, TPS and token mix
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@deckhand.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 22:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deckhand dedicated pool — post-demo recap and sizing asks

Hi Oliver — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the follow-ups we promised: 

Call highlights
- Use case: real-time agent orchestration + customer-facing summarization for mobile and web.
- Target endpoints: high-concurrency chat (web) + async batch summarization.
- Initial rollout region: US-east, prefer private VPC for sensitive PII flows but open to hybrid (hosted API for low-risk traffic).

Open items we need to size Dedicated correctly
1) TPS targets: can you confirm steady-state RPS/TPS during business hours and peak TPS? We need both 95th and burst estimates.
2) Token mix: please attach a 24-hour sample if possible (avg tokens per request, 95p tokens, prompt vs completion split).
3) Concurrency expectations: how many simultaneous active conversations do you expect? Is session affinity required?
4) Latency SLO: target p95 latency for chat (in ms) and any hard max.
5) Security: confirm whether all inference must stay in VPC/on-prem or if a split route (hosted for non-PII) is acceptable.

I've attached a capacity worksheet (deckhand_capacity_worksheet.xlsx) with our baseline questions and a sample token CSV for reference. If you can populate the token sample and add any internal scaling windows (e.g., marketing blasts), that helps.

Quick thoughts from our team (high level)
- If you have burst windows >2x steady TPS, we'll propose a dedicated pool with burst slots + warm instances to meet p95 SLOs.
- GPU family impacts per-token cost and latency (A100 vs H100 tradeoffs) — we'll propose a split pool if you need strict latency for chat and lower-cost for offline summarization.

Next steps
- Can you fill the attached token sample and return by EOD Tue so we can produce a sizing worksheet?
- Suggest a 45-minute sizing workshop on Wed to walk the worksheet with your infra/procurement people.

Thanks — Marissa

Subject: Re: Deckhand dedicated pool — post-demo recap and sizing asks

Marissa — thanks for the clear notes and the worksheet. A few quick answers and one ask: 

Answers
- Steady-state TPS: ~35 TPS across our web endpoints during business hours.
- Peak TPS: typically spikes to ~130 TPS during product update rollouts (lasting ~8-12 minutes).
- Tokens: attaching a 12-hour export (deckhand_token_sample.csv). Rough averages: prompt ~260 tokens, completion ~420 tokens; 20% of calls are long-form (>1500 tokens).
- Concurrency: we expect 400+ simultaneous active sessions during peak; session affinity preferred for stateful agents.
- Latency: p95 target for chat is <250ms; we can accept 400ms soft max.
- Security: PII must remain in VPC for at least the first 6 months of the pilot. Non-PII can go through hosted API.

Ask
- Can you outline cost delta between A100 and H100 for this workload (rough $/token delta or $/hour estimate)? Procurement will need a ballpark for their internal finance review.

I'll aim to fill the worksheet over the weekend — happy to stand up the sizing workshop Wed if you can make it.

—Oliver

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Deckhand dedicated pool — post-demo recap and sizing asks

Thanks Oliver — good detail in the token sample, that helps. Some quick engineering notes to set expectations for the workshop: 

GPU family guidance (short):
- H100: best p95 latency for high-concurrency chat, faster decoding for large models (recommended if p95 latency <250ms strict). Higher $/hour but fewer instances needed for tight SLOs.
- A100: cost-effective for heavy throughput and mixed workloads; slightly higher latency for the same model size vs H100. Good fit for mixed chat + offline summarization pools.
- L4 / T4 class: viable for smaller models or high-volume embedding workloads, not ideal for large-chat p95 SLOs.

Sizing heuristics (based on sample)
- Using your average token numbers and 130 TPS bursts, baseline estimate: 6 H100 instances sized with continuous batching + 3 warm burst instances to cover 2x spikes with <400ms p95.
- Alternatively, 12 A100 instances with heavier batching can meet the same throughput but expect p95 to move closer to ~320–380ms under peak unless we raise concurrency limits and KV cache affinity.
- For 20% long-form calls (>1500 tokens), factor ~25–30% additional token cost and longer per-request GPU time; consider a dedicated batch lane for long-form jobs to avoid harming chat p95.

Operational recommendations:
- Use session-affinity routing for chat to keep KV caches hot — reduces token compute on subsequent messages.
- Configure autoscaling based on request queue depth + token backlog rather than raw TPS to better capture long-form jobs.
- Reserve a small Dedicated burst pool (hot standby) for deployment-time spikes; billed at reserved discounted rate if committed.

I'll prep a quick worksheet variant with 2 pool options (H100-lean for latency vs A100-cost-optimized) for the workshop. Ben, can you pull sample cost delta numbers to include in the deck?

-Karthik
